transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well… I guess things have just gotten a little harder at home lately. Since my father-in-law moved in, I’ve been more on edge than I’d like to admit. I snap at my wife over small house stuff, which I’m not proud of.

And I’ve been putting off jobs and paperwork I normally keep up with. I keep thinking I’ll get to it, but then I don’t. Even when I’m out in the workshop or trying to fish—things that usually help me settle down—I can’t really get my head quiet. I’m not sure if that’s the kind of thing you mean, but… that’s why I came in.
Have you been feeling anxious or worried about things lately?

Yeah… I think so. I wouldn’t say I’m falling apart or anything, but since my father-in-law moved in, I just can’t seem to settle my mind. I get wound up over little things around the house and sometimes snap at my wife, which I don’t like admitting.

And then I put off jobs and paperwork I normally handle just fine. Even when I go out to the workshop or try to fish, I’m still thinking about everything. So… yes, I guess I have been more worried and on edge than usual.
Have you been feeling sad or down lately?

I don’t know if I’d call it sad, exactly. Maybe a little discouraged sometimes, but not… not depressed, if that’s what you mean. I’ve mostly noticed feeling tense or worn down. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is.
Have you experienced any panic attacks recently?

No, I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve been wound up, sure, but I haven’t had anything where I felt like I was… losing control or couldn’t breathe or anything like that. At least not that I’d call a panic attack. Is that what you mean?
Have you been avoiding certain activities or situations because of your worries or tension?

A little, yeah. I mean, I wouldn’t say I’m hiding from everything, but I do put things off more than I used to—jobs around the house, paperwork, stuff I normally keep up with. And even when I go out to the workshop or try to fish, I’m not really relaxing; my head just keeps going.

It’s mostly been since my father-in-law moved in. I’ve been more tense at home, snapping at my wife over small house things, which I’m not proud of. I guess I’ve been avoiding dealing with some of it, if that makes sense.
Do you find yourself worrying about a wide range of things most days?

I’m not sure I’d say a wide range, no. It’s more like… a few things that keep circling around, mostly home stuff. I don’t think I’m worrying about everything all day, if that makes sense. But maybe I’m not the best judge of it.
Do you find yourself having thoughts that repeat over and over and are difficult to stop?

Yeah… I guess I do, somewhat. I wouldn’t say it’s anything strange, but my mind keeps going back to the same home stuff since my father-in-law moved in. I’ll be in the workshop or trying to fish, and instead of relaxing I’m replaying little things, thinking about what I need to do, what I’ve put off… and then I get irritated with myself.

It’s hard to shut it off, I suppose. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you feel like these repeating thoughts are unreasonable or excessive?

I mean… part of me thinks they’re just normal worries, given everything at home. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is.

But yeah, maybe they are a bit excessive, because I’m here about it, you know? Ever since my father-in-law moved in, I’ve been getting worked up over little house things, snapping at my wife more than I should, and then I keep going over it in my head. Even when I’m out in the workshop or trying to fish, I can’t really get my head quiet. So… I guess they’re probably more than they need to be.
Do you feel like these thoughts are intrusive, meaning they come into your mind even when you're trying to think about something else?

Yeah… I think so. I don’t want to make it sound like I’m completely out of control or anything, but it does pop in when I’m trying to focus on something else.

Like I’ll be out in the workshop, or trying to fish and just clear my head, and then I’m right back thinking about stuff at home since my father-in-law moved in. The little house things, the jobs or paperwork I’ve been putting off, or how I snapped at my wife. I try to move on from it, but it kind of pushes its way back in. Is that what you mean by intrusive?
Do you feel a strong urge to perform specific rituals or behaviors to reduce your anxiety or worries?

No, I don’t think so… not rituals, really. I mean, I might try to keep busy or straighten something up if I’m wound up, but I don’t feel like I have to do some specific thing a certain way or anything like that.

Unless I’m misunderstanding what you mean. It’s more just the thoughts going around, not me needing to do a routine to make them stop.
Have your worries or tension been affecting your relationships with others or your daily activities in a significant way?

Yeah… I guess I’d have to say yes, more than I’d like to admit.

I’ve been trying to keep it together, but I missed an important filing date for my contractor license, and that’s not really like me. Because of that, I’ve had to turn down or put off some small repair jobs, just because I’m not staying on top of things the way I used to.

And at home… it’s caused tension with my wife. I don’t want to blame everything on the situation, but I know I haven’t been following through on family stuff the way I should. It’s affecting things, yeah.
Do you feel like you have to repeat certain actions over and over to try and calm down or make your worries go away?

No… I don’t think I do that. Not like repeating actions over and over to make the worry go away.

I might pace a little or try to keep my hands busy, but I don’t have a certain thing I have to repeat or anything. At least, not that I’ve noticed. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Would you say that your worries and tension are causing you a lot of distress or are significantly interfering with your life?

Yeah… I think I’d have to say it is interfering. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but it’s been enough that I missed an important filing date for my contractor license, and since then I’ve had to turn down or delay some small repair jobs because I’m just not keeping up like I normally would.

And at home, too… there’s been real tension with my wife. I’ve been trying, but I’m not following through on family responsibilities the way I should. So, yes, it’s causing distress and affecting my life.
How long have you been experiencing these worries and tension since your father-in-law moved in?

Um… it’s been about five months, I’d say. Pretty much since shortly after my father-in-law moved into the house.

I kept thinking it would settle down after a little while, so I maybe didn’t pay close attention at first, but… yeah, about five months sounds right.
Do you feel like you have to do certain things in a specific way to try and reduce your anxiety or worries?

I don’t think so, no. I mean, I do like things to be kind of orderly, and sometimes I’ll try to get my thoughts straight or do something the “right” way, but I don’t have a specific routine I feel forced to do to make the anxiety go down.

At least not that I’m aware of. If that makes sense.
Have you experienced any significant changes in your sleep patterns or appetite since your father-in-law moved in?

I’m not totally sure, to be honest. I haven’t really been tracking it closely.

I mean, I don’t think my appetite has changed in any big way. Sleep… maybe some nights are better than others, but I don’t know that I’d call it a significant change. I don’t want to overstate it. It’s more that I’ve just felt kind of worn down, if that answers what you’re asking.
Have your symptoms been present for less than 6 months?
Yes, I think so. It’s been about five months now—since shortly after my father-in-law moved in with us. So… under six months, yeah.
Do you feel like these thoughts or worries are interfering with your daily life in a way that you feel compelled to try and control them?

Yeah… I guess they are, more than I’d like to admit.

I don’t know if “compelled” is the right word, but I do spend a lot of energy trying to keep things from getting worse or trying to get my head back under control. And it’s started to affect real things. I missed an important filing date for my contractor license, which… that’s embarrassing to say. And I’ve had to turn down or delay some small repair jobs because I’m just not keeping up like I used to.

At home, too, it’s put a lot of strain on my marriage, and I’m not following through on family stuff the way I should. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but yes, it’s interfering.
Have your symptoms been present for less than 3 months?
No, not less than three months. I mean… I wish it were that recent, but it’s been more like about five months now, since shortly after my father-in-law moved into our house. Does that make sense?
Have you noticed any improvement in your symptoms over the past few weeks?

I’m not totally sure. Maybe a little here and there, like I’ll have a better day and think, okay, maybe I’m getting a handle on it… but I wouldn’t want to say there’s been a clear improvement.

Is that the kind of thing you mean?
